gloss: setting sail; departure (of a ship or aircraft)

definitions.gloss: setting sail; departure (of a ship or aircraft)
definitions.explanation: A ship or aircraft leaving on a voyage. The focus is on the start of the journey rather than on the act of leaving a particular harbor.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}が{出航|しゅっこう}した。
{台風|たいふう}のため{出航|しゅっこう}が{延期|えんき}された。
examples.english: The departure was postponed because of the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{九時|くじ}に{出航|しゅっこう}する{予定|よてい}なので、{一時間前|いちじかんまえ}には{乗|の}ってください。
examples.english: We are scheduled to sail at nine in the morning, so please board an hour beforehand.

notes:
{出|しゅつ} (go out) + {航|こう} (voyage, navigation). Used as a noun and with する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出航|しゅっこう}する: to set sail
- {出航|しゅっこう}{時刻|じこく}: departure time
- {出航|しゅっこう}を{見合|みあ}わせる: to hold off on sailing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出港|しゅっこう}: leaving port — a homophone that focuses on the ship leaving the harbor itself; often interchangeable in practice
- {出発|しゅっぱつ}: departure — the general word, used for any traveler or vehicle
- {入港|にゅうこう}: entering port — the opposite movement
